I guess it depends on what you mean by "from scratch". If I say I made a cake from scratch, most people would assume I mixed together flour, baking powder, baking soda, some salt, some eggs, maybe some cocoa powder and so on... as opposed to using a box mix of some sort. One could argue, however, that the flour was itself a processed food, which is why hippie friends of mine mill their own flour from whole grain they purchase from a local co-op. I didn't raise my own laying chickens for the eggs either. I certainly didn't create my own salt (NaCl) by mixing together hydrochloric acid (HCl) and sodium hydroxide (NaOH), which is super dangerous so don't try it at home.

So, we are back to what does "from scratch" mean. If the goal is to produce a human-like being by hand-crafting every bit of a sperm and egg from base molecules, fertilize the egg with the sperm, and then gestate the result in some sort of mechanical womb, I imagine this is quite a ways off. If you're willing to settle for a donor egg fertilized with a donor sperm which has had its genes artificially synthesized and then implant that in a human womb for gestation, the technology is probably closer than you think.

Consider what technology advances we've made in the last 100 years and then try to imagine the next 100. It's pretty amazing.
